### TP-RVFI-017: Fault on the second half of a misaligned access: one record, first-half address
- Features: F-RVFI-014
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: PMP region boundary placed so the first half is allowed and the second denied;
  also data_err_i on the second transaction only.
- Stimulus: misaligned loads/stores straddling the boundary or with the second response errored.
- Randomized: direction, size (half/word), boundary placement, error source.
- Knobs: knob:pmp_regime (sparse), knob:dmem_err_rate (rare)
- Fire-check: >= 10 misaligned records with rvfi_trap = 1 whose first transaction completed
  without error on the dbus (for stores the first-half write reached memory) and whose second
  half faulted: for the data_err_i source the dbus monitor shows the errored second transaction;
  for the PMP source the second half NEVER reaches the bus (data_req_o = data_req_out &
  ~pmp_req_err[PMP_D], rtl/ibex_core.sv:1063; fact-check TP-RVFI-017, UNOBSERVABLE), so the
  PMP case is identified by "first half completed, no second request issued, rvfi_trap = 1 with
  mcause 5/7 and the TB PMP model denying the second-half address". >= 5 of each source.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_rvfi_proto (single record; mem_addr == first (misaligned) address; masks
  0) ; gen_isa_compare with the Q-DL-7 policy (memory compared after the handler; the partial
  first-half write is an accepted RTL detail; mtval = the word-aligned second-half address per
  TP-RVFI-016) ; gen_chk_dbus_proto (no second request for the PMP source) ; gen_chk_pmp.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_rvfi_trap
- Bins: CG-RVFI-002.cr_trap_half.load_yes_second, CG-RVFI-002.cr_trap_half.store_yes_second,
  CG-RVFI-002.cr_trap_half.load_yes_first, CG-RVFI-002.cr_trap_half.store_yes_first,
  CG-RVFI-002.cp_fault_half.second, CG-RVFI-002.cp_fault_half.first

### TP-RVFI-018: ID-stage exception coinciding with a WB load/store fault: the WB error wins, the ID instruction is killed and re-executed
- Features: F-RVFI-015
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: a load/store that will fault in WB (data_err_i with 1..4 cycles of latency, or a
  PMP fault on the second half of a misaligned access) immediately followed by an instruction that
  raises an ID exception (illegal instruction, ecall, ebreak with dcsr.ebreakm/u = 0, U-mode CSR
  violation); the handler logs mcause/mepc and returns to mepc, so the killed instruction
  re-executes and traps again.
- Stimulus: 200+ such pairs with latencies swept so the ID exception request coincides with the WB
  exception (the TB timing model of the two instructions decides which pairs coincide).
- Randomized: ID cause, latency, load vs store, privilege.
- Weights: W-CAUSE, W-LS
- Knobs: knob:dmem_rvalid_delay (short), knob:dmem_err_rate (frequent), knob:pmp_regime (sparse)
- Fire-check: >= 5 coincident pairs (TB model) where the WB fault's trap record (mcause
  ExcCauseLoadAccessFault / ExcCauseStoreAccessFault, mepc read in the handler = the load/store PC)
  is followed directly by the handler's first record, and after the handler's mret the ID
  instruction re-executes and produces its own record (rvfi_pc_rdata = the ID instruction's PC,
  rvfi_trap = 1, mcause = its own cause).
- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare (priority: the WB fault is taken first, mepc = the load/store PC,
  the ID instruction has no architectural effect before the handler and executes after mret; order
  continuity) ; gen_chk_rvfi_proto (no record for the killed ID instruction between the WB trap
  record and the handler's first record). The RVFI-record confirmation (two trap records in order,
  B14 convention note) is TP-RVFI-039 (informational).
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_rvfi_trap
- Bins: CG-RVFI-004.cr_wb_coincident.wb_yes_no, CG-RVFI-004.cr_wb_coincident.wb_no_no,
  CG-RVFI-004.cr_wb_coincident.id_no_no, CG-RVFI-004.cp_coincident_wb_err.yes,
  CG-RVFI-004.cp_coincident_wb_err.no, CG-RVFI-004.cp_missing_record.no

### TP-RVFI-019: rvfi_ext_irq_valid is a level announcing the interrupt entry with the captured mip/nmi/nmi_int/debug_req state
- Features: F-RVFI-016
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: interrupts enabled; NMI handler; integrity injection for internal NMI.
- Stimulus: interrupts arriving with the pipeline idle (during WFI, after a fence) and busy (mid
  straight-line code, and with a load outstanding in WB so that ID empties before WB drains);
  external and internal NMIs; debug requests (which never raise the marker: rvfi_irq_valid needs
  ~new_debug_req, rtl/ibex_core.sv:1965).
- Randomized: timing, lines, source, dmem latency of the load preceding the interrupt.
- Knobs: knob:irq_regime (sparse), knob:irq_line_mix (with_nmi), knob:dmem_err_rate (rare),
  knob:debug_req_regime (sparse), knob:dmem_rvalid_delay
- Fire-check: >= 20 rising edges of rvfi_ext_irq_valid, each with rvfi_valid low on every cycle of
  the marker's high window and followed by a handler first record (rvfi_intr = 1) one cycle after
  the marker falls; rvfi_ext_pre_mip nonzero (containing the taken line) for irq cases,
  rvfi_ext_nmi for external NMIs, rvfi_ext_nmi_int for internal ones; >= 3 high windows of length
  1 (same-cycle gnt, next-cycle rvalid on the handler fetch) and >= 3 longer than 1; >= 3
  interrupt entries WITHOUT a marker (ID emptied before WB drained: the irq arrived while a load
  was outstanding in WB, so captured_valid was already set when ready_wb came, :1965) whose
  handler first record carries the captured pre_mip / nmi state; per seed the minimum observed
  distance from the last pre-interrupt record's rvfi_valid to the marker's rising edge equals the
  bring-up-pinned constant GEN_RVFI_IRQ_MARKER_OFFSET (predicted 3: record at decision + 1, marker
  at decision + 4; C-13, C-16).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_irq (C-13 / X-16: rvfi_ext_irq_valid is a LEVEL that rises at decision +
  4 (rvfi_irq_valid flop, stage [0], [1], [2], rtl/ibex_core.sv:1965-1971, :1992-2002,
  :2134-2141, :2192-2199), stays high until about two cycles after the handler's first
  instruction enters ID (stage [0] is rewritten only when a new instruction enters ID) and never
  coincides with rvfi_valid; every interrupt entry is announced by AT MOST ONE marker rising edge,
  and an entry without a marker is legal only when ID emptied before WB drained; the captured
  pre_mip contains the taken line either on the marker or on the handler's first record) ;
  gen_chk_nmi ; gen_isa_compare (the shim takes the interrupt at the announced boundary, or at the
  handler's first record when no marker was generated).
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_rvfi_ext
- Bins: CG-RVFI-003.cr_irq_collision.yes_no,
  CG-RVFI-003.cr_irq_collision.no_no, CG-RVFI-003.cr_irq_kind.yes_no_no, CG-RVFI-003.cr_irq_kind.yes_yes_no,
  CG-RVFI-003.cr_irq_kind.yes_no_yes,
  CG-RVFI-003.cp_irq_valid.yes, CG-RVFI-003.cp_irq_valid.no, CG-RVFI-003.cp_marker_len.one,
  CG-RVFI-003.cp_marker_len.two_plus, CG-RVFI-003.cp_entry_marker.yes,
  CG-RVFI-003.cp_entry_marker.no, CG-RVFI-003.cp_marker_offset.min,
  CG-RVFI-003.cp_marker_offset.more

### TP-RVFI-021: rvfi_ext_debug_req and rvfi_ext_debug_mode
- Features: F-RVFI-018
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: debug ROM with dret; debug_req_i level policy.
- Stimulus: debug requests during straight-line code, during handlers, while a load is
  outstanding in WB (request arriving on an empty ID), while in debug mode (ignored), with
  dcsr.step; the pin is released at a random point inside the debug ROM (level policy until the
  hart halts, then random release).
- Randomized: timing, step, release point.
- Knobs: knob:debug_req_regime (sparse), knob:dmem_rvalid_delay
- Fire-check: >= 10 debug entries via debug_req_i, each with: the record in ID at the pin's rise
  carrying rvfi_ext_debug_req = 0 and completing (its dpc-relation: dpc read in the debug ROM ==
  the pc_rdata of the first post-dret record, C-3), no record between it and the first debug-ROM
  record, and the first debug-ROM record carrying debug_req = 1 and debug_mode = 1; >= 100 records
  with debug_mode = 1; >= 5 debug-ROM records with the pin already released (debug_req = 0,
  debug_mode = 1); >= 3 entries whose request arrived on an empty ID (captured_debug_req path).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_debug (C-3 / X-6: rvfi_ext_debug_req is sampled at the instruction's
  IF->ID transfer with the live pin, or from captured_debug_req when the request arrived on an
  empty ID (rtl/ibex_core.sv:1949-1957, :1996-2001); a high debug_req_i lets no new instruction
  transfer into ID outside debug mode because halt_if is combinational from the request
  (rtl/ibex_controller.sv:700-708, :1020), so a record with debug_req = 1 and debug_mode = 0
  never exists: the instruction in ID at the rise reports 0 and completes, an instruction whose
  transfer would follow the rise never enters (entry with dpc = its pc, no record), and the first
  debug-ROM record reports 1; debug_mode == the core's debug state when the instruction left ID:
  the first debug-ROM record has debug_mode = 1, the first post-dret record 0) ; gen_isa_compare.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_rvfi_ext
- Bins: CG-RVFI-003.cr_dbg.yes_yes, CG-RVFI-003.cr_dbg.no_yes, CG-RVFI-003.cr_dbg.no_no,
  CG-RVFI-003.cp_debug_req.yes, CG-RVFI-003.cp_debug_req.no

### TP-RVFI-024: rvfi_ext_rf_wr_suppress set only on loads whose completing beat had an integrity error
- Features: F-RVFI-021
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: as TP-SEC-008: the injected integrity errors hit only the beat that completes
  the load (aligned, or the second half of a misaligned load); the first-beat class is
  TP-RVFI-040 (expected-fail, B16), excluded here (C-8).
- Stimulus: injected load integrity errors on completing beats plus normal loads, stores and
  errored (data_err_i) loads.
- Randomized: as TP-SEC-008.
- Knobs: knob:dmem_err_rate (rare), knob:dmem_rvalid_delay
- Fire-check: >= 5 records with rf_wr_suppress = 1 (>= 2 aligned, >= 2 second-half) and >= 1000
  with 0 including >= 10 data_err_i load traps.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_bus_intg_rsp (suppress == 1 iff the record is a load whose COMPLETING
  beat had an integrity error (rvfi_rf_wr_suppress = instr_done_wb & ~rf_we_wb & outstanding_load
  & lsu_load_resp_intg_err, rtl/ibex_core.sv:2384-2385, keyed on the data_intg_err of the current
  rvalid, rtl/ibex_load_store_unit.sv:697-698); 0 on data_err_i traps and stores) ;
  gen_chk_rvfi_proto (rd_addr == 0 when suppress == 1).
- Notes: comparator convention the landing-2a runs surfaced, since BUILT (the LOG-037c condition was met when 1c landed at 9e912bb and passed both reviewers, cross-model APPROVE-WITH-CHANGES and the Critic's tb_l1c at fb8137e, whose hold answers are T-136 may lift and T-137 may lift FOR BUS-ERROR ARMING with T-183 owed to 2b, T-183 lifting later under LOG-074. The irq_entry bound convention is not one 1c carried: tb_l1c Section 4 leaves it as fu2a M-5 owed to 2b, and the Critic closed it at landing 7 by the per-line release and the end-of-run rule with MUT-NT and MUT-NT2; dv/auto_dv/evidence/gen_tdd_step2b.md Section 8): a load whose response carried an integrity error retires with rvfi_ext_rf_wr_suppress = 1 and the DUT keeps the destination's old value (rtl/ibex_core.sv:2383-2385: rvfi_rf_wr_suppress_wb = instr_done_wb and not rf_we_wb_o and outstanding_load_wb and lsu_load_resp_intg_err). The 2a acceptance is NOT credited: it rested on the DUT's flag alone (the model's write undone and the rd compare skipped whenever the DUT asserted it), so a DUT that spuriously drops a load's register write would be accepted; T-183 (tb-infra 2c at cbadb7f, reviewed APPROVE-WITH-CHANGES; LOG-074) gates the undo on an announced corruption for that load and compares the DUT's rd fields against no write; integrity runs were consistency-only until then and compare fully since, the CM117-M-1 spanning-load gap being an over-strict open item.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_sec_alert_inject_dbus
- Bins: CG-RVFI-003.cp_rf_wr_suppress.yes, CG-RVFI-003.cp_rf_wr_suppress.no

### TP-RVFI-035: rvfi_ext_irq_valid never coincides with a retiring record (negative check)
- Features: F-RVFI-032
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: interrupts enabled.
- Stimulus: interrupt asserted so that the pipeline-empty decision cycle lands as close as
  possible to the WB completion of the last pre-interrupt instruction (sweep the assertion cycle
  over a window around loads of varying latency); also the pipeline-idle case (WFI, fence).
- Randomized: latency, line, instruction before the interrupt.
- Knobs: knob:irq_regime (sparse), knob:dmem_rvalid_delay
- Fire-check: >= 10 interrupt entries whose marker rising edge was observed, with the last
  pre-interrupt record's rvfi_valid at most GEN_RVFI_IRQ_MARKER_OFFSET cycles before it in >= 3
  of them (the closest achievable spacing); per seed the minimum observed spacing equals the
  bring-up-pinned constant GEN_RVFI_IRQ_MARKER_OFFSET (predicted 3, C-13 / C-16).
- Pass criteria: T-044 property sva_rvfi_irq_valid_exclusive / gen_chk_irq: rvfi_valid and
  rvfi_ext_irq_valid are NEVER both high in the same cycle (fact-check TP-RVFI-035,
  UNREACHABLE-PRECONDITION, X-16: the decision needs ~instr_valid_id & ready_wb, so the last
  pre-interrupt record is out by decision + 1 while the marker passes four flops and rises at
  decision + 4, and the handler's first record comes one cycle after the marker falls; no
  instruction retires in between, rtl/ibex_core.sv:1965-1971, :1985-2004, :2192-2198); the
  interrupt is still announced at most once; the record fields and the marker's pre_mip / nmi /
  debug_req are both trustworthy because they never share a cycle (Q-DL default 10 closed by
  X-16) ; gen_isa_compare.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_rvfi_ext
- Bins: CG-RVFI-003.cr_irq_collision.yes_no, CG-RVFI-003.cp_collision.no,
  CG-RVFI-003.cp_marker_offset.min, CG-RVFI-003.cp_entry_marker.yes

### TP-RVFI-039: RVFI record convention on a WB-error / ID-exception coincidence: two trap records in order (B14 confirmation)
- Features: F-RVFI-015
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: as TP-RVFI-018 (shared run).
- Stimulus: as TP-RVFI-018.

- Fire-check: for >= 5 coincident pairs the trace shows exactly two trap records in program order:
  first the WB fault record (rvfi_trap = 1, the load/store PC), then, after the handler's records,
  the re-executed ID instruction's own record (rvfi_trap = 1, its PC, its own cause), with zero
  records for the killed instance in between.

  killed ID instruction's record appears as the re-executed instance; rtl/ibex_core.sv:1851-1853
  suppresses only the killed instance). A single record for the pair re-opens B14 (bug log B14;
  rtl-arch T-041 fact-check row 48); until the confirmation simulation is recorded the item is
  informational and excluded from the pass gate.
- Expected: informational (B14 confirmation; excluded from the pass gate)

## New checkers requested
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

- gen_chk_rvfi_proto (NEW, requested): RVFI self-consistency checker, independent of the ISA
  model. Rules: rvfi_order increments by exactly 1 (64-bit) and restarts at 1 after reset;
  rvfi_valid is a one-cycle pulse per order value; pc_rdata[n+1] == pc_wdata[n] unless rvfi_intr
  on n+1, a trap record at n, a debug entry between them, or a FLUSH-redirect record (mret, dret,
  trap) at n, whose pc_wdata is the next sequential fetch address (C-1 / X-1: compared as
  pc_rdata + length, never as the target; the target is pc_rdata[n+1]; fence.i's pc_wdata is
  pc + 4 either way); rd_wdata == 0 when rd_addr == 0; rd_addr == 0 on trap records; rs*_rdata
  == 0 when rs*_addr == 0; rs3_addr == 0 on single-cycle instructions, == instr[31:27] on ternary
  records and == the rs1 field on other multi-cycle records (TP-RVFI-009); on records DECODED as
  loads or stores exactly one of rmask/wmask is nonzero when rvfi_trap = 0 and both are 0 on
  WB-trap records, mask values only {0001, 0011, 1111} at bit 0 and mem_addr == the effective
  address; on every other record (ALU, CSR, branch, jump, ID-stage trap) the mem fields are
  ignored (rmask = 4'b1111 and addr = the ALU result are the B18 garbage, C-12); insn[31:16] == 0
  when insn[1:0] != 11; rvfi_halt == 0; rvfi_ixl == 1; rvfi_mode in {0, 3} and changes only after
  a trap / mret / dret record or on the first record after an interrupt or debug entry
  (TP-RVFI-007); rvfi_intr == 1 iff an interrupt/NMI vector was set since the previous record
  (RTL-defined meaning; a debug entry landing between IRQ_TAKEN and the handler's first ID cycle
  puts the flag on the debug-ROM's first record, TP-RVFI-006); rvfi_ext_irq_valid is a level that
  never coincides with rvfi_valid and rises at most once per interrupt entry (C-13);
  rvfi_ext_debug_req = 1 never occurs with rvfi_ext_debug_mode = 0 (C-3);
  no record carries the dummy encoding class at a PC outside the program image (dummies never on
  RVFI); expanded_insn_last exactly once per Zcmp sequence with the same pc_rdata on every
  micro-op; exactly one rd write per record, from the source implied by the instruction class
  (ALU / CSR / mul-div -> WB flop, load -> LSU return, stores / branches / traps none;
  F-RVFI-034); no instruction in program order is missing from the trace (B14 detector, needs the
  program image and the model's order). Disable knob +gen_chk_rvfi_proto_en=0. Mutation classes:
  RVFI pipeline plumbing, order/valid gating, dummy gating, mask derivation.
- gen_test_dit_* (cocotb test-level fire-checks): gen_test_dit_branch, gen_test_dit_div,
  gen_test_dit_mul, gen_test_dit_handover, gen_test_dit_lsu, gen_test_dit_dummy,
  gen_test_dit_dummy_div, gen_test_dit_seed - gap-histogram assertions named in the items; these
  are test-level Python assertions, not new SV checkers.
- gen_test_rst_values / gen_test_rst_boot (cocotb): reset-value and boot-timing assertions.
- gen_chk_alerts extension: per-injection accounting (exactly one alert_minor_o pulse per
  injected ICache ECC error; alert_major_bus_o pulse count == corrupted rvalid beat count) and
  the in-reset rule (bus alert may follow corrupted beats during reset; the other two never).
- gen_chk_bus_intg_rsp per-beat rule (C-8, B16): the load-suppression prediction keys on the beat
  that COMPLETES the access; a misaligned load with only its first beat corrupted is classified as
  the B16 class (documented intent: suppress; RTL: rd written), reported through the expected-fail
  items TP-SEC-040 / TP-RVFI-040 and never counted as a pass elsewhere; the internal-NMI latency
  bound is two ordinary instructions (C-7, D21) and its mtval is lsu_addr_last at the corrupted
  beat.
- gen_chk_fetch_en rule (C-4): no new icache line allocation after the Off edge; remaining beats
  of open fill buffers are legal; instr_req_o == 0 whenever core_busy_o == Off; gen_chk_ibus_proto
  keeps "req held until gnt" with no fetch_enable tolerance.
- gen_chk_debug extension: "RTL-documenting" mode for the step-consumes-a-dummy case (accept a
  step re-entry with unchanged dpc only when P1 shows a dummy) and for trap/debug entry while
  fetch is disabled (Q-DL-8).
- gen_chk_crash_dump: the RVFI-derived model must include the WritebackStage offset (current_pc
  is the ID PC, one instruction ahead of the retiring record) and the misaligned rule for
  last_data_addr (word-aligned second-half address).

# 4.8 Areas REG, XIF, ADOPT: Randomization layers (regime knobs and schedule), cross-interface crosses, bins adopted from riscv-dv


Task: T-006 cross-cutting subagent. Companion: fcov_xcut.md (covergroups CG-REG/CG-XIF/CG-ADOPT,
sampling model S1..S20, completeness measure). Build configuration `opentitan`; DUT gen_dut_top
(README_T006_BRIEF.md). Feature references are to dv/auto_dv/docs/gen_feature_list.md, which superseded the draft;
protocol rules to dv/auto_dv/evidence/gen_interface_inventory.md (s11 and the per-interface
sections); agents and knobs to the committed component API documents (gen_component_api_env_knobs.md and the per-agent ones), which superseded tb-infra's scoping notes b.1-b.6 and c.4.

This area owns the three randomization layers of DV_prompt.txt Section 6 (per-transaction
distributions live in each agent and are cited per knob below; regime knobs and the regime
schedule are defined here) and the global set of cross-interface crosses. Area subagents
reference the knobs by name; this file is the definition.

## Conventions applied in this part (plan v2b; README_FIX3_BRIEF.md C-1..C-16, rtl-arch T-053 X-rules)

- C-1 (X-1) A redirect target of a trap / mret / dret record is observed as the NEXT record's
  rvfi_pc_rdata (or the DmExceptionAddr / DmHaltAddr / vector fetch with the icache off); the
  rvfi_pc_wdata of those records is the next sequential fetch address and is never asserted as the
  target. Only branch/jump records carry the target in rvfi_pc_wdata (fcov_xcut.md S19). Zcmp precision (rtl-arch R9, dv/auto_dv/evidence/gen_t102_rtl_facts.md; the Critic's T-102c verdict corrects its earlier "length 2"): a trapping Zcmp micro-op record reports rvfi_pc_wdata == rvfi_pc_rdata (trap-record offset 0, neither insn_len nor 2, because expansion holds the fetch) and the whole sequence restarts from its first micro-op after mret; the comparator rule is TB Infra's T-102c (T-134).
- C-3 (X-6/X-7) Interrupt and debug entry wait for an empty ID and a ready WB: the instruction
  already in ID when the request arrives completes first; mepc / dpc = pc of the first
  not-yet-executed instruction, derived from the last retired record (nominal 2 records after the
  pin edge, worst case GEN_IRQ_ENTRY_BOUND_RECORDS / GEN_DBG_ENTRY_BOUND_RECORDS = 17). Every XIF
  "same cycle" cross samples the coincidence at the pins (S18 back-dated) and attributes the
  outcome by the next record(s); "dpc = next pc" in an item means this rule.
- C-4 (X-5) fetch_enable_i != On stops only NEW icache lookups (rtl/ibex_core.sv:648 gates req_i,
  consumed only by lookup_req_ic0, rtl/ibex_icache.sv:249): the remaining beats of fill buffers
  allocated before the Off edge keep requesting (fill_ext_req :756 has no req_i term; a request
  awaiting grant is held, :764). Checker rule (gen_chk_fetch_en): no new line allocation after the
  Off edge (every instr_req_o inside the Off window addresses a remaining beat of a line open at the
  edge); no request is ever withdrawn; instr_req_o == 0 whenever core_busy_o == Off; no retirement
  after the in-flight instructions drain.
- C-5 (X-8) A stepped WFI (dcsr.step = 1, not in debug mode) never reaches WAIT_SLEEP (FLUSH ->
  DBG_TAKEN_IF, rtl/ibex_controller.sv:985-987) and core_busy_o stays On; an unstepped WFI gives
  exactly one ctrl_busy = 0 cycle in WAIT_SLEEP (:598-604), visible on core_busy_o only with no
  fetch beat outstanding, no invalidation and an idle LSU. A dip of <= 1 cycle is never sleep.
- C-6 (X-9) A synchronous exception clears mstatus.MIE at the trap entry
  (rtl/ibex_cs_registers.sv:924) and irq_enabled = MIE | (priv == U) (rtl/ibex_controller.sv:490):
  a pending ORDINARY interrupt is taken only after the handler's mret (MIE <- MPIE) or an explicit
  MIE write; an NMI ignores MIE (:498-500, outside NMI mode) and a debug request ignores it too:
  both are taken in the first empty-ID DECODE after the exception's FLUSH, before the handler's
  first instruction.
- C-7 (X-10, D21) Up to two ordinary records (more with Zcmp) may follow a corrupted load's record
  before the internal-NMI marker; checkers follow the RTL.
- C-8 (X-11, B16) A misaligned LOAD whose FIRST beat carries an integrity error still writes rd
  (alert and internal NMI fire); the rd-write rule for that class is B16, owned by the mem area's
  expected-fail split of TP-DMEM-041. Items here that inject data integrity errors (TP-REG-026,
  TP-XIF-003) do not gate on rvfi_ext_rf_wr_suppress for a corrupted first beat.
- C-13 (X-16) rvfi_ext_irq_valid is a LEVEL rising four cycles after the decision cycle, not a
  pulse; no S-state, fire-check or bin of this area uses it: interrupt entry is anchored on the
  rvfi_intr record and the vector fetch (fcov_xcut.md S18).
- C-14 A fire-check that infers "in ID" or "no bus fetch of the target" from the instruction bus
  pins cpuctrlsts.icache_enable = 0 or derives the redirect from RVFI; "outstanding at ID entry"
  (TP-XIF-004, TP-XIF-010) is derived from RVFI record spacing only (fcov_xcut.md S21).
- C-15/C-16 Every item of this area is `pass` (no expected-fail or informational item); every
  fire-check is a per-seed assertion on an observable.

## Part 1: regime knobs (layer 2) and the regime schedule (layer 3)

### Knob conventions

- Name: `knob:<name>`; value set as listed; one value is in force per phase (TB-side knobs) or
  per program region (program-side knobs: instr_mix, priv_regime, pmp_regime).
- Command-line controls are the codegen forms only (gen_tb_architecture.md 8.3 item 4 and 8.3a;
  single source dv/auto_dv/tb/gen_tb_knobs.yaml, rendered by gen_knobs_codegen.py): layer 2
  `+gen_knob_<name>=<value>` (one plusarg per knob, 20 regime knobs, value strings identical to the
  bin names of the knob definitions below); a knob given on the command line is PINNED: it holds
  that value for the whole run (every phase and region), the schedule generator removes it from its
  draws and the agent logs `pinned = 1` in its phase-log record; pinning any subset of knobs is
  legal. Layer 3 `+gen_regime_sched=<knob>:<value>@r<N>|c<N>,...` (r = retirement-count trigger,
  c = cycle-count trigger). There is no schedule seed plusarg, no per-agent regime plusarg and no
  separate pin plusarg; the retired forms appear nowhere in this area. The numeric layer-1 window
  overrides of gen_tb_knobs.yaml (`+gen_ibus_gnt_min/max`, `+gen_dbus_rvalid_min/max`,
  `+gen_ibus_err_rate`, ...) are TB Infra debug knobs and are never used by a plan item.
- Regime schedule seed: none of its own. Absent `+gen_regime_sched`, Python derives the schedule
  deterministically from the single run seed (RANDOM_SEED = +ntb_random_seed = program seed,
  DV_prompt Section 6 "Seeds") and echoes it in the time-0 banner, so test name + seed reproduce
  the schedule; supplied, the string is CONSUMED as the schedule (gen_tb_architecture.md 4.2, XM-L5),
  so one schedule replays under another data seed by copying the echoed string.
- T-181 (LOG-042a, root cause LOG-042c, lifted LOG-042e, 2026-09-03): the 3e template's schedule runner applied only the idx=0 knobs at
  start-up and never a mid-run phase, on any test and any tree (its EOT wait ended at the first report-word store); the Test Writer's
  3h (9500268) fixed it and passed both reviewers. Caveats: a seed whose mid-run triggers all fall after the end of test passes with
  no mid-run phase applied, so a mid-run bin can stay unhit on a PASS and the fcov gate is where that shows; the promotion's
  layers-live evidence (l9g) exercised the initial phase only, which the promoted tests' measured status does not depend on; the
  items the hold covered (this area's gen_reg_* groups, every *regime* group and the items whose stimulus names a mid-run regime
  change, gen_test_plan.md Section 0) sit in unbuilt groups, so the lift credits none of them today.
- Default: the value in force when a test does not enable the schedule (Phase-1 feature-targeted
  tests) and no pin is given. Phase-2 tests draw every knob per phase from the value set
  (uniform unless stated); the default is not favoured, so randomness does not collapse into one
  typical case.
- Phase log: every agent writes one record per phase {phase_idx, knob, applied_value,
  start_cycle, start_rvfi_order, pinned}; the record carries the APPLIED value read back from the
  driver, which is what the fire-checks and CG-REG-* sample.
- Layer 1 (per-transaction) is inside each agent and is cited under "Layer 1" per knob and in the
  Layer-1 weight tables below; layer 2 selects the distribution; layer 3 (the schedule) selects
  the sequence of layer-2 values.

### Layer-2/3 command-line names (knob table)

The command-line name of every knob is its codegen plusarg `+gen_knob_<name>=<value>`
(gen_tb_knobs.yaml, kind enum; the value strings ARE the bin names below), the schedule is
`+gen_regime_sched`, and the CG-REG-* covergroups sample the value the agent APPLIED. The table
lists, per knob, the plusarg, the agent that consumes it and the layer-1 window it selects
(regime_windows in gen_tb_knobs.yaml; numeric overrides exist as TB Infra debug plusargs only).
Program-side knobs are consumed by the Python program generator, which writes the region tuple to
the phase-marker register; their region boundaries are program markers, not `+gen_regime_sched`
triggers. NOTE (Q-11): gen_tb_knobs.yaml renders the absent-plusarg defaults short / short / quiet /
single for imem_gnt_delay, imem_rvalid_delay (dmem likewise), irq_regime and irq_line_mix where the
knob definitions below say random / random / sparse / multi; the plan defaults are the Phase-1
intent and the DV Lead reconciles them with TB Infra.

Items of every area cite these rows by knob value instead of repeating weights (Critic S-6). Each
row is the per-transaction draw inside the class the layer-2 knob selects; layer 3 sequences the
classes. TB Infra implements the rows as `dist` constraints in the agents' items.

| | short | uniform 1..3 |
| | long | 90% uniform 4..32, 10% uniform 33..128 |
| | random | 40% 0, 40% uniform 1..3, 20% uniform 4..32 |
| ibus / dbus response latency (imem_rvalid_delay, dmem_rvalid_delay) | min1 | 1 cycle: 100% |
| | short | uniform 1..3 |
| | long | 90% uniform 4..32, 10% uniform 33..128 |
| | random | 40% 1, 40% uniform 1..3, 20% uniform 4..32 |

| bus integrity corruption (imem_intg_err_rate, dmem_intg_err_rate) | none / rare / frequent | Bernoulli 0 / ~1/512 / ~1/20 per response; 1-bit vs 2-bit flip 50/50 |

### Knob definitions

Instruction memory agent (tb-infra b.1; protocol gen_interface_inventory s2 rules 1-6):

- knob:imem_gnt_delay {same_cycle, short, long, random}; default random. Selects the
  instr_gnt_i latency distribution after instr_req_o (rule 1: req held until gnt, addr stable;
  rule 2: same-cycle gnt legal; F-IMEM-001/003/004/005).
  same_cycle: gnt in the request cycle for 100% of requests (F-IMEM-004; also exercises the
  no-combinational-path rule F-IMEM-029). short: uniform 1..3 cycles (F-IMEM-005). long: uniform
  4..32 cycles with 10% in 33..128 (long waits expose redirect-while-waiting-for-grant
  F-IMEM-017 and WFI with a fetch outstanding F-RST-017). random: per-request mix 40% same-cycle,
  40% 1..3, 20% 4..32. Layer 1: the per-request draw inside the selected class.
- knob:imem_rvalid_delay {min1, short, long, random}; default random. Selects the
  instr_rvalid_i latency after grant (rule 3: never in the grant cycle, exactly one per grant,
  in order; F-IMEM-006/007/009). min1: exactly 1 cycle (fastest legal; back-to-back
  F-IMEM-010, fill data timing F-IC-016). short: 1..3. long: 4..32 with 10% 33..128 (drives the
  outstanding depth toward the cap, F-IMEM-008). random: 40/40/20 mix. Layer 1: per-beat draw;
  every beat carries correct inverted 39/32 SECDED bits (rule 4) regardless of knob.
- knob:imem_err_rate {none, rare, frequent}; default none. Probability that a response beat
  carries instr_err_i = 1 (F-IMEM-011..015, F-EXC-003). none: 0. rare: ~1/512 beats. frequent:
  ~1/20 beats. Layer 1: per-beat Bernoulli draw; the erroring beat still carries valid SECDED
  (integrity corruption is a separate directed injection, see Open questions Q-1). Errors on
  speculative beats that are never executed must produce no exception (F-IMEM-012).
- knob:imem_outstanding_cap {1, 2, 4, 8}; default 8. Maximum granted-but-unanswered beats the
  agent accepts before withholding instr_gnt_i (RTL bound NUM_FB*IC_LINE_BEATS = 8, s2). The
  value set is {1, IC_LINE_BEATS, 2*IC_LINE_BEATS, NUM_FB*IC_LINE_BEATS}; the bin labels
  cap1/cap2/cap4/cap8 are these expressions for this configuration. 1: one beat at a time
  (serialised fills). 2: one line. 4: two lines. 8: never withholds for depth; a 9th outstanding
  beat is a DUT protocol violation caught by gen_chk_ibus_proto. Layer 1: gnt draw is then
  gated by the cap.
- knob:imem_intg_err_rate {none, rare, frequent}; default none (DV Lead addition; Q-1 resolved).
  Probability that a response beat's SECDED field instr_rdata_i[38:32] is corrupted (1 or 2 bits,
  50/50; +gen_ibus_intg_err_rate per mille, regime intg_err). none: 0. rare: ~1/512 beats.
  frequent: ~1/20 beats. Effect: alert_major_bus_o in the rvalid cycle and an instruction access
  fault if the word is executed; no NMI on the instruction side (D14; F-IMEM-027). Layer 1:
  per-beat Bernoulli draw and bit pattern.

Data memory agent (tb-infra b.2; protocol s3 driver rules 1-8):

- knob:dmem_gnt_delay {same_cycle, short, long, random}; default random. data_gnt_i latency
  (rule: gnt only while req; F-DMEM-001/002/004/005). Same classes as imem_gnt_delay; the second
  half of a misaligned pair draws its own grant delay (F-DMEM-024).
- knob:dmem_rvalid_delay {min1, short, long, random}; default random. data_rvalid_i latency
  (F-DMEM-006/007/010; both halves in flight F-DMEM-025, first rvalid with second grant in the
  same cycle F-DMEM-026). long creates the windows for interrupt/debug/WFI while a data access is
  outstanding (F-IRQ-017, F-DBG-003, F-DMEM-030/031). Every response, loads and stores alike,
  carries correct SECDED (rule 4); stores get a fixed rdata with a valid code (rule 3).
- knob:dmem_err_rate {none, rare, frequent}; default none. Probability of data_err_i = 1 per
  response (F-DMEM-021..023/036/037, F-EXC-025/027). none: 0. rare: ~1/512. frequent: ~1/20.
  Layer 1: per-response draw, with a 50/50 pick of first/second half when the response belongs
  to a misaligned pair; after a first-half error the second half is still served (rule 7).
- knob:dmem_intg_err_rate {none, rare, frequent}; default none (DV Lead addition; Q-1 resolved).
  Probability that data_rdata_i[38:32] is corrupted on a load or store response (1 or 2 bits,
  50/50; +gen_dbus_intg_err_rate per mille, regime intg_err). none: 0. rare: ~1/512. frequent:
  ~1/20. Effect: alert_major_bus_o and the internal NMI (mcause 0xFFFFFFE0; up to two ordinary
  records may retire before its marker, D21 / C-7); rd is suppressed only when the COMPLETING beat
  carries the error: a corrupted FIRST beat of a misaligned load writes rd (B16, C-8; the class is
  owned by the mem area's expected-fail split of TP-DMEM-041) (F-IRQ-040, F-SEC-015/016,
  F-DMEM-041). Layer 1: per-response Bernoulli draw and bit pattern.

Interrupt driver (tb-infra b.5; s6):

- knob:irq_regime {quiet, sparse, storm}; default sparse. Rate of assertion events. quiet: no
  new events (lines already asserted follow their hold policy). sparse: geometric inter-arrival,
  mean ~2000 cycles, at most one event outstanding. storm: mean ~100 cycles (gen_tb_knobs.yaml regime_windows.irq_event_mean.storm at 4d48d84, TB Infra landing 2a: at a mean of 20 the interrupt program livelocked, every retirement an entry, dv/auto_dv/evidence/gen_tdd_step2b.md Section 8), overlapping events,
  immediate re-assertion after the handler ack (F-IRQ-011 drain by priority, F-IRQ-027 re-trap
  after mret, F-EXC-059 trap storm). Layer 1: inter-arrival draw and per-event line choice.
- knob:irq_line_mix {single, multi, fast_only, with_nmi}; default multi. Which lines an event
  asserts (levels, s6). single: one of the 3 + $bits(irq_fast_i) maskable lines, uniform. multi:
  a random subset of 2..k lines at once (priority F-IRQ-009/010). fast_only: irq_fast_i lines
  only, 1..15 at once (lowest index wins F-IRQ-010; fast 0 and 14 vectors F-IRQ-061/062).
  with_nmi: as multi plus irq_nm_i with probability 25% (F-IRQ-030/034; internal NMI is a
  directed integrity injection, not this knob).
- knob:irq_hold {until_taken, through_handler, pulse}; default until_taken. Deassert policy
  (levels; a one-cycle pulse can be missed, s11). until_taken: hold until rvfi_intr is observed,
  release within 0..3 cycles (F-IRQ-002). through_handler: hold until the handler acks via the
  TB MMIO irq-ack store (b.8); returning without ack re-traps (F-IRQ-027, F-IRQ-052).
  pulse: 1..3 cycle pulse regardless of taking, may be dropped (F-IRQ-025 no spurious trap,
  F-IRQ-026). gen_chk_irq relaxes its entry-bound check for pulse and keeps the no-spurious-trap
  check.

Debug request driver (tb-infra b.6; s7):

- knob:debug_req_regime {none, sparse, storm}; default none. none: never asserted. sparse: mean
  ~5000 cycles; level held until rvfi_ext_debug_mode rises, then released within 0..3 cycles;
  50% of events keep the level high through dret to re-halt (F-DBG-007). storm: mean ~100
  cycles, including 20% one-cycle pulses that may be dropped (F-DBG-005) or land in FLUSH
  (F-DBG-006, B9 owned by the DBG area). Layer 1: inter-arrival and hold draws.

fetch_enable driver (s1):

- knob:fetch_enable_regime {always_on, toggling}; default always_on. always_on: IbexMuBiOn for
  the phase. toggling: Off windows of 1..200 cycles at random intervals (mean gap ~1000 cycles);
  the Off encoding is 80% IbexMuBiOff and 20% an invalid MuBi encoding, never X (F-IMEM-022..025,
  F-IMEM-023 invalid encoding behaves as Off, F-RST-010..015, F-SEC-012).

Instruction-cache RAM models and scramble-key responder (tb-infra b.3, b.4; s5):

- knob:icache_ecc_err_rate {none, rare, frequent}; default none. Injection into
  ic_tag_rdata_i / ic_data_rdata_i on lookups (F-IC-030..035). none: 0. rare: ~1/2000 lookups.
  frequent: ~1/50 lookups (intent figures; as built the rates are none 0 / rare 2 / frequent 50 per mille,
  regime_windows.rate_per_mille in gen_tb_knobs.yaml). Layer 1 per injection: tag vs data 50/50, 1-bit vs 2-bit 50/50, way
  uniform over IC_NUM_WAYS. Built in tb-infra landing 11 at f28d09b as test equipment for the tag RAMs
  only, one bit per injection, announced through gen_icram_events (before it the knob had no consumer
  and no retained run had alert_minor_o high); the data-RAM and two-bit halves are BUILT in tb-infra landing 14 at a28d1ae (WP-12, Section 2a).
  Effective only while the program has enabled the cache: CG-REG-005
  credits the knob bins only with icache_en_q (`iff`, S12), so a phase with the cache disabled
  contributes no sample; the alert/invalidation effects belong to the IC area.
- knob:scr_key_delay {immediate, delayed, withheld_then_valid}; default immediate. Latency from
  the ic_scr_key_req_o pulse to ic_scr_key_valid_i = 1 (level answering a one-cycle pulse, s11;
  F-IC-008/023). immediate: valid low for exactly 1 cycle. delayed: low 2..200 cycles.
  withheld_then_valid: low 201..2000 cycles, long enough for a second fence.i (F-IC-024) and a
  WFI while the cache is busy (F-IC-029); the run still progresses (F-IC-010 "never" is a
  directed test).

Wrapper pin ties (run constants, not scheduled):

- knob:mcounteren_writable {on, off, invalid}; default on (DV Lead addition). MuBi value tied to
  mcounteren_writable_i for the whole run: IbexMuBiOn, IbexMuBiOff, or a random other
  $bits(ibex_mubi_t) encoding (plusarg `+gen_knob_mcounteren_writable`). Writes to mcounteren
  land only when the pin is exactly IbexMuBiOn (rtl/ibex_cs_registers.sv:845, F-SEC-020,
  F-PMC-025); the class is sampled at the first retired mcounteren write (CG-REG-010).

Program generator (riscv-dv driven from Python; program-side knobs switch at region boundaries,
where the generated program stores the region tuple to the TB phase-marker register, b.8):

- knob:instr_mix {isa_only, m_heavy, compressed_heavy, bitmanip_heavy, csr_heavy, ls_heavy,
  branch_heavy, mixed}; default mixed. Instruction-category weights of the region. isa_only:
  RV32I only. m_heavy: ~40% mul/div (F-MUL). compressed_heavy: ~60% Zca/Zcb/Zcmp incl. cm.push/
  pop sequences (F-CMP). bitmanip_heavy: ~40% from the legal RV32BOTEarlGrey set
  (gen_rv32b_otearlgrey_encodings.md, F-BIT-001). csr_heavy: ~30% CSR ops incl. 2% illegal
  accesses (F-CSR). ls_heavy: ~50% loads/stores, 30% misaligned (F-DMEM-015). branch_heavy:
  ~40% branches/jumps in short loops (F-ISA-023). mixed: flat weights. Layer 1: riscv-dv's
  per-instruction operand/immediate randomization.
- knob:priv_regime {m_only, u_heavy, alternating}; default m_only. m_only: all M-mode.
  u_heavy: ~70% of instructions in U-mode (mret to U, ecall back). alternating: mode switch
  every 10..100 instructions (F-PRV-002/003/006, F-IRQ-008 U-mode interrupts ignore MIE).
- knob:pmp_regime {off, sparse, dense, mml_on}; default off. PMP configuration written by the
  region prologue. off: all A = OFF, mseccfg = 0 (U-mode code then faults on every access,
  F-PMP-053; the generator keeps U excursions short). sparse: 2..4 of PMPNumRegions regions
  (TOR/NAPOT) covering code/data/stack. dense: all PMPNumRegions regions, NA4/NAPOT/TOR mixed,
  <= 25% locked (never the code region), overlapping (F-PMP-045/046). mml_on: mseccfg.MML = 1
  (+MMWP 50%, RLB 50%) with a dense MML-legal set (F-PMP-056..065). MML and MMWP are sticky
  (F-PMP-023/024), so transitions out of mml_on are unreachable within a reset epoch and reachable
  only across a mid-run reset, where mseccfg clears (F-PMP-015): CG-REG-006 keeps the three
  mml_on_to_* bins as legal bins owned by TP-REG-028 (gen_xif_reset).

### Regime schedule (layer 3)

- Per test the schedule generator (Python, from the single run seed; emitted as the
  `+gen_regime_sched` string and echoed in the banner) draws K phases, K in {1, 2, 3..4, 5+} with
  weights 10/20/40/30; for each phase a full tuple of the 19 scheduled knob values (the 17 brief
  knobs plus imem_intg_err_rate and dmem_intg_err_rate; pinned agents fixed; mcounteren_writable
  is a run constant) and a duration class {short, medium, long} with weights 40/40/20.
- TB-side knobs (imem_* incl. imem_intg_err_rate, dmem_* incl. dmem_intg_err_rate, irq_*,
  debug_req_regime, fetch_enable_regime, icache_ecc_err_rate, scr_key_delay) change at cycle-timed
  boundaries (`c<N>` triggers): short = 500..2000
  cycles, medium = 2001..20000, long = 20001..100000. The boundary is a TB event independent of
  program progress, so it can fall inside WFI, debug mode, a Zcmp sequence or a bus wait.
- Program-side knobs (instr_mix, priv_regime, pmp_regime) change at region boundaries measured in
  retired instructions: short = 100..500, medium = 501..5000, long = 5001..20000; the region
  prologue writes the tuple to the phase-marker register (one store), which the data agent
  forwards to the phase log.
- Transition rule: at a TB-side boundary every TB-side knob is redrawn; knobs whose value did not
  change are not transitions. Existing in-flight items keep the regime they were issued under
  (an outstanding response keeps its scheduled latency; an asserted irq line keeps its hold
  policy); the new regime applies to new requests/events.
- A reset test (gen_xif_reset) continues the schedule across a mid-run reset: the phase index
  keeps counting, the reset is logged as an event, and the region after the reset starts a new
  reset epoch. mseccfg (MML/MMWP/RLB) clears at reset (F-PMP-015), so pmp_regime transitions out of
  mml_on are reachable only there: gen_xif_reset constrains >= 1 mml_on region to end in a reset
  and generates a non-mml_on region after it (TP-REG-028; CG-REG-006 cp_pmp_regime_tr.mml_on_to_*).
- Sampling rule for the regime bins (fcov_xcut.md Phase log): CG-REG value and `_tr` bins are
  credited at the phase's FIRST regime-relevant event (first granted request, first assertion
  edge, first injection; an activity threshold for absence-type values), never at the phase start,
  so a transition is never credited before a transaction ran under the new value.
- Duration and phase-count bins, transition bins and in-flight-transition bins: CG-REG-007 and
  CG-REG-008.

### TP-REG-001: knob:imem_gnt_delay covers every value and every transition
- Features: F-IMEM-001, F-IMEM-003, F-IMEM-004, F-IMEM-005, F-IMEM-017
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: none (M-mode program, icache_enable randomized by the program)
- Stimulus: program through the fetch bus with instr_mix = mixed; the imem agent runs a sweep schedule that visits every value of knob:imem_gnt_delay for at least one phase (K >= 4, order randomized), per-request grant latency drawn inside the selected class
- Randomized: value order, phase durations, other imem/dmem knobs per phase, program content, seed
- Knobs: knob:imem_gnt_delay
- Fire-check: cocotb assertion over the phase log and the ibus monitor's per-phase grant-latency histogram (phases with >= 20 granted requests): every v in {same_cycle, short, long, random} was applied for >= 1 such phase, and in every such phase the MEASURED histogram class equals the applied value (same_cycle: 100% of grants at latency 0; short: 100% in 1..3 with >= 2 distinct values; long: 100% in 4..128 and, with >= 200 requests, >= 1 in 33..128; random: latency 0, 1..3 and 4..32 each observed), so the check is measured DUT-side traffic against the echo, not echo against schedule [export-rows: ibus gnt; ibus req; regime phase] (source: +gen_export_file E lines, architecture Section 9; RVFI-only fallback: the per-phase rvfi_ext_mcycle gap distribution class of the records versus the applied value)
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_ibus_proto, gen_sva_ibus (req held until gnt, addr stable while waiting, no gnt without req); gen_isa_compare (program results independent of fetch timing); gen_chk_regime (applied == scheduled per phase)
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_reg_knob_sweep
- Bins: CG-REG-001.cp_imem_gnt_delay.same_cycle, CG-REG-001.cp_imem_gnt_delay.short, CG-REG-001.cp_imem_gnt_delay.long, CG-REG-001.cp_imem_gnt_delay.random, CG-REG-001.cp_imem_gnt_delay_tr.same_cycle_to_short, CG-REG-001.cp_imem_gnt_delay_tr.same_cycle_to_long, CG-REG-001.cp_imem_gnt_delay_tr.same_cycle_to_random, CG-REG-001.cp_imem_gnt_delay_tr.short_to_same_cycle, CG-REG-001.cp_imem_gnt_delay_tr.short_to_long, CG-REG-001.cp_imem_gnt_delay_tr.short_to_random, CG-REG-001.cp_imem_gnt_delay_tr.long_to_same_cycle, CG-REG-001.cp_imem_gnt_delay_tr.long_to_short, CG-REG-001.cp_imem_gnt_delay_tr.long_to_random, CG-REG-001.cp_imem_gnt_delay_tr.random_to_same_cycle, CG-REG-001.cp_imem_gnt_delay_tr.random_to_short, CG-REG-001.cp_imem_gnt_delay_tr.random_to_long, CG-REG-001.cr_gnt_x_rvalid.same_cycle_min1, CG-REG-001.cr_gnt_x_rvalid.same_cycle_short, CG-REG-001.cr_gnt_x_rvalid.same_cycle_long, CG-REG-001.cr_gnt_x_rvalid.same_cycle_random, CG-REG-001.cr_gnt_x_rvalid.short_min1, CG-REG-001.cr_gnt_x_rvalid.short_short, CG-REG-001.cr_gnt_x_rvalid.short_long, CG-REG-001.cr_gnt_x_rvalid.short_random, CG-REG-001.cr_gnt_x_rvalid.long_min1, CG-REG-001.cr_gnt_x_rvalid.long_short, CG-REG-001.cr_gnt_x_rvalid.long_long, CG-REG-001.cr_gnt_x_rvalid.long_random, CG-REG-001.cr_gnt_x_rvalid.random_min1, CG-REG-001.cr_gnt_x_rvalid.random_short, CG-REG-001.cr_gnt_x_rvalid.random_long, CG-REG-001.cr_gnt_x_rvalid.random_random, CG-WIT-001.cp_clause.w_tp_reg_001

- Features: F-DMEM-001, F-DMEM-002, F-DMEM-004, F-DMEM-005, F-DMEM-024
- Phase: 1

### TP-XIF-014: CSR write pipeline flush x interrupt pending (incl. writes that enable or disable it)
- Features: F-CSR-006, F-CSR-007, F-CSR-008, F-CSR-026, F-CSR-031, F-CSR-033, F-IRQ-059, F-IRQ-060, F-EXC-061
- Phase: 2
- Tier: full
- Preconditions: csr_heavy regions writing mie/mstatus/mip/mscratch/mepc/mtvec/cpuctrlsts with random values (mtvec base kept valid)
- Stimulus: random regime with irq_regime storm, irq_hold through_handler, irq_line_mix multi
- Randomized: CSR, value, arrival instant, seed
- Knobs: knob:irq_regime, knob:irq_hold, knob:irq_line_mix, knob:instr_mix
- Fire-check: >= 1 flushing CSR write whose commit cycle (its RVFI record cycle - GEN_CSR_WRITE_TO_RVFI_OFFSET = 2, S18) has irq_pending_o = 1, >= 1 non-flushing (mscratch/mepc) write likewise, >= 1 mie write after which irq_pending_o rose in the cycle BEFORE the write's RVFI record (record - 1: the mie update is visible on the pin one cycle after the commit, so the edge precedes the record; a window "after the record" never samples) and the next record is the handler, and >= 1 mie write after which it fell in that cycle and the next record is sequential [export-rows: misc irq_pending] (source: +gen_export_file E lines, architecture Section 9; RVFI-only fallback: the CSR write record followed by the handler record (rvfi_intr) or a sequential record; mie / mip read-back)

### TP-XIF-017: reset asserted mid-run x each in-flight class
- Features: F-RST-001, F-RST-008, F-RST-009, F-RST-018, F-RST-019, F-RST-024, F-RST-026, F-SEC-035, F-IC-009, F-IC-022, F-DBG-008, F-IRQ-055, F-RVFI-033

- Tier: full
- Preconditions: none (the program is re-booted after each reset from boot_addr_i + 0x80)
- Stimulus: rst_ni asserted at randomized instants (1..64 cycles low) chosen to land in each in-flight class (the reset test samples the monitors and fires when a target class is observed); the memory model DROPS every response still owed for a pre-reset request at release (S3 / Q-010: the LSU and the icache have no outstanding-request qualifier, rtl/ibex_load_store_unit.sv:694-697, so an unsolicited rvalid after release would be consumed as a response: rf_we pulse, a spurious access fault on data_err_i, alert_major_bus_o on bad integrity; responses delivered while rst_ni is still low are harmless and may be drained); debug_req_i / irq_nm_i randomly held across release
- Randomized: reset instant, length, in-flight class, hold across release, seed

- Fire-check: >= 1 mid-run reset per in-flight class of CG-XIF-010.cp_inflight observed in the falling-edge cycle; after release the first instr_addr_o is the boot vector within 2 cycles (fetch on), all outputs sit at reset values in the first cycle, and the dbus/ibus monitors see zero rvalid pulses between release and the first post-reset grant on that bus; per seed the model logged >= 1 dropped pre-reset response (CG-XIF-010.cp_after.stale_rsp_after_release samples that DROP event, never a delivery: the RTL would consume a stale response, fact-check TP-XIF-017) [export-rows: ibus req; ibus rvalid; dbus rvalid; ibus gnt; dbus gnt] (source: +gen_export_file E lines, architecture Section 9; RVFI-only fallback: the first post-reset record rvfi_pc_rdata == the boot vector with rvfi_order restarted; no record of a pre-reset in-flight instruction after release)
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_reset (new: reset values of every output, boot fetch, stale-response DROP policy: no rvalid on either bus without a post-reset grant); gen_chk_alerts (no alert_major_bus_o after release: nothing stale reaches the DUT); gen_chk_crash_dump (reset values); gen_isa_compare (restart from the reset state)
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_xif_reset

### TP-XIF-019: PMP reconfiguration x in-flight fetch / cached code / following data access
- Features: F-PMP-055, F-PMP-065, F-PMP-066, F-PMP-079, F-PMP-092, F-PMP-093, F-PMP-100, F-IC-039, F-PRV-013, F-CSR-006
- Phase: 2
- Tier: full
- Preconditions: pmp_regime in {sparse, dense, mml_on}; the program rewrites PMP CSRs mid-region so that the verdict for the next instruction or the next data word flips; icache enabled in some regions so the affected code is already cached
- Stimulus: random regime with imem_rvalid_delay long (prefetches outstanding at the write), imem_outstanding_cap 8, priv_regime alternating
- Randomized: CSR, new verdict, lock bits, icache state, seed
- Knobs: knob:pmp_regime, knob:imem_rvalid_delay, knob:imem_outstanding_cap, knob:priv_regime
- Fire-check: >= 1 PMP CSR write retirement with ibus_outst >= 1 after which the next record traps with an instruction access fault at the write's pc_wdata, >= 1 after which the next load/store faults with no bus request, and >= 1 with the icache enabled where the faulting instruction had been fetched from the cache (no bus request for its word since the last invalidation)
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_pmp (verdict applies to the very next fetch and data access; denied data never on the bus); gen_chk_csr_readback (locks, sticky bits); gen_isa_compare

### TP-XIF-021: dummy instruction inserted x branch redirect / interrupt / debug request (coverage-only, probe P1)
- Features: F-DIT-011, F-DIT-012, F-DIT-013, F-DIT-019, F-DIT-020, F-DIT-021, F-DIT-023, F-DIT-028, F-DIT-029, F-FE-018, F-PMP-094, F-TRG-026
- Phase: 2
- Tier: full
- Preconditions: cpuctrlsts.dummy_instr_en = 1 with dummy_instr_mask swept over all 8 values by region; secureseed written at random points
- Stimulus: random regime with irq_regime storm, debug_req_regime sparse, branch_heavy regions, dmem_rvalid_delay long (loads outstanding when dummies enter ID)
- Randomized: mask, seed writes, event timing, seed
- Knobs: knob:irq_regime, knob:debug_req_regime, knob:dmem_rvalid_delay, knob:instr_mix, knob:priv_regime
- Fire-check: probe P1 dummy_instr_id rose >= 1 time in the S19 redirect cycle (rvfi_valid - GEN_RVFI_ID_EXIT_OFFSET of the redirecting record), >= 1 time with irq_pending_o = 1, >= 1 time with debug_req_i = 1 and >= 1 time with a load outstanding; RVFI shows no record for any dummy and the architectural stream is unchanged
- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare (dummies invisible: no RVFI record, register file unchanged); gen_chk_irq / gen_chk_debug (mepc / dpc = the next real instruction); gen_chk_counters as bounds (B7 minstret counting of dummies is owned by the PMC area's F-PMC-011 item)
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_xif_dummy

### TP-XIF-022: icache ECC error injected x concurrent fill, invalidation, redirect or cache disable
- Features: F-IC-030, F-IC-031, F-IC-032, F-IC-033, F-IC-035, F-IC-027, F-IC-041, F-IC-028, F-SEC-001
- Phase: 2
- Tier: full
- Preconditions: cpuctrlsts.icache_enable toggled by the program mid-region (F-IC-041)
- Stimulus: random regime with icache_ecc_err_rate in {rare, frequent}, imem_rvalid_delay long, branch_heavy regions, fence.i sprinkled
- Randomized: injection target (tag/data, way, bits), concurrent event, seed
- Knobs: knob:icache_ecc_err_rate, knob:imem_rvalid_delay, knob:scr_key_delay
- Fire-check: >= 1 ECC injection on a lookup while fill_inflight, >= 1 while invalidating, and >= 1 cpuctrlsts.icache_enable clearing write retired while fill_inflight; each injection that hit a valid lookup produced exactly one alert_minor_o pulse and the RAM model saw the invalidating tag write and a refill from the bus
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_icache (invalidate + refill + one minor alert; disabled cache fetches everything from the bus, no backfill); gen_chk_alerts; gen_isa_compare
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_xif_random
- Bins: CG-XIF-005.cp_event.ecc_inject, CG-XIF-005.cp_event.icache_disable, CG-XIF-005.cr_event_x_fill.ecc_inject_one_beat_outst, CG-XIF-005.cr_event_x_fill.ecc_inject_two_to_line, CG-XIF-005.cr_event_x_fill.ecc_inject_multi_line, CG-XIF-005.cr_event_x_fill.icache_disable_one_beat_outst, CG-XIF-005.cr_event_x_fill.icache_disable_two_to_line, CG-XIF-005.cr_event_x_fill.icache_disable_multi_line, CG-XIF-005.cr_event_x_inval.ecc_inject_none, CG-XIF-005.cr_event_x_inval.ecc_inject_invalidating, CG-XIF-005.cr_event_x_inval.icache_disable_none, CG-XIF-005.cr_event_x_inval.icache_disable_invalidating, CG-XIF-005.cr_event_x_key.ecc_inject_valid, CG-XIF-005.cr_event_x_key.icache_disable_valid

### TP-REG-026: Bus integrity-error injection knobs (DV Lead addition after area review)
- Features: F-IMEM-027, F-SEC-017, F-SEC-019, F-DMEM-041
- Phase: 2
- Tier: full
- Preconditions: MemECC=1 wrapper (Q-002 default); program with mixed loads/stores and fetches
- Stimulus: memory agents corrupt the 7-bit SECDED field of instr_rdata_i / data_rdata_i at the
  rate selected by knob:imem_intg_err_rate / knob:dmem_intg_err_rate {none, rare, frequent}
  (single-bit and double-bit patterns randomized per injection)
- Randomized: which response is corrupted, bit pattern, phase in which the knob changes
- Knobs: knob:imem_intg_err_rate, knob:dmem_intg_err_rate
- Fire-check: every value of both knobs was applied for >= 1 phase with >= 200 integrity-checked
  responses on that bus; MEASURED per such phase: none -> zero corrupted beats and zero
  alert_major_bus_o pulses attributable to that bus; rare -> corrupted/total in [1/2048, 1/128];
  frequent -> in [1/80, 1/5]; every corrupted beat is followed by an alert_major_bus_o pulse in
  its response cycle (both sides same-cycle exact, GEN_ALERT_BUS_WINDOW = 0, gen_tb_architecture.md
  8.2 item 3); the sweep visits every ordered pair of consecutive values per knob (K >= 7) [export-rows: dbus rvalid; ibus rvalid; alert alert_major_bus; regime phase] (source: +gen_export_file E lines, architecture Section 9; RVFI-only fallback: the per-phase rvfi_ext_nmi_int entry count (record count per C-7) and rvfi_trap (mcause 1) counts versus the applied rate class)
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_bus_intg_rsp (alert_major_bus_o per injection; D-side internal NMI with
  mcause 0xFFFFFFE0 within 0..2 ordinary records (D21 / C-7) and rvfi_ext_rf_wr_suppress = 1 when the
  COMPLETING beat carries the error; a corrupted FIRST beat of a misaligned load is the B16 class
  (C-8): recorded here, gated only by the mem area's expected-fail item; I-side fetch fault, no NMI
  per D14); gen_chk_alerts; gen_chk_regime
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_xcut_regime_sweep
- Bins: CG-REG-009.cp_imem_intg_rate.none, CG-REG-009.cp_imem_intg_rate.rare, CG-REG-009.cp_imem_intg_rate.frequent, CG-REG-009.cp_imem_intg_rate_tr.none_to_rare, CG-REG-009.cp_imem_intg_rate_tr.none_to_frequent, CG-REG-009.cp_imem_intg_rate_tr.rare_to_none, CG-REG-009.cp_imem_intg_rate_tr.rare_to_frequent, CG-REG-009.cp_imem_intg_rate_tr.frequent_to_none, CG-REG-009.cp_imem_intg_rate_tr.frequent_to_rare, CG-REG-009.cp_dmem_intg_rate.none, CG-REG-009.cp_dmem_intg_rate.rare, CG-REG-009.cp_dmem_intg_rate.frequent, CG-REG-009.cp_dmem_intg_rate_tr.none_to_rare, CG-REG-009.cp_dmem_intg_rate_tr.none_to_frequent, CG-REG-009.cp_dmem_intg_rate_tr.rare_to_none, CG-REG-009.cp_dmem_intg_rate_tr.rare_to_frequent, CG-REG-009.cp_dmem_intg_rate_tr.frequent_to_none, CG-REG-009.cp_dmem_intg_rate_tr.frequent_to_rare, CG-REG-009.cr_intg_rates.none_none, CG-REG-009.cr_intg_rates.none_rare, CG-REG-009.cr_intg_rates.none_frequent, CG-REG-009.cr_intg_rates.rare_none, CG-REG-009.cr_intg_rates.rare_rare, CG-REG-009.cr_intg_rates.rare_frequent, CG-REG-009.cr_intg_rates.frequent_none, CG-REG-009.cr_intg_rates.frequent_rare, CG-REG-009.cr_intg_rates.frequent_frequent, CG-WIT-001.cp_clause.w_tp_reg_026

### TP-REG-028: knob:pmp_regime transition out of mml_on across a mid-run reset
- Features: F-PMP-023, F-PMP-024, F-PMP-015
- Phase: 2
- Tier: full
- Preconditions: the region running when the reset fires was generated with pmp_regime = mml_on (its prologue wrote mseccfg.MML = 1, MMWP/RLB randomized) and read mseccfg back; the re-booted program's first region is generated with pmp_regime in {off, sparse, dense} and reads mseccfg before its prologue writes it
- Stimulus: gen_xif_reset schedule constrained so that >= 1 mid-run rst_ni assertion (1..64 cycles low) falls inside an mml_on region and the schedule continues across the reset (Regime schedule rule); the post-reset regime is drawn from {off, sparse, dense}
- Randomized: reset instant inside the mml_on region, reset length, post-reset regime, MMWP/RLB values, region contents, seed
- Knobs: knob:pmp_regime, knob:priv_regime, knob:imem_rvalid_delay, knob:dmem_rvalid_delay
- Fire-check: the program-side phase log shows a region with applied_value = mml_on immediately followed (reset logged between them) by a region with applied_value in {off, sparse, dense}, both regions having reached their first retirement (CG-REG-006 activity rule); RVFI shows a csrr mseccfg record with MML = 1 before the reset and the first mseccfg read after release returning 0 before the new prologue's write; gen_chk_pmp's model rebuilt from the retired writes shows MML = 0 in the new region
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_reset (mseccfg and every PMP CSR at reset values after release, F-PMP-015); gen_chk_csr_readback (MML/MMWP sticky before the reset, cleared by it); gen_chk_pmp (post-reset verdicts computed with MML = 0); gen_isa_compare
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_xif_reset
- Bins: CG-REG-006.cp_pmp_regime_tr.mml_on_to_off, CG-REG-006.cp_pmp_regime_tr.mml_on_to_sparse, CG-REG-006.cp_pmp_regime_tr.mml_on_to_dense

## New checkers requested

- gen_chk_regime (TB self-check, not a DUT checker): for every phase and knob, the applied value
  logged by the agent equals the scheduled value; pinned knobs never change; phase durations fall
  in their class; no knob changes outside a boundary; the phase log is complete (one record per
  phase per agent). Fails through uvm_error; disable knob +gen_chk_regime_en=0. Needed by every
  TP-REG fire-check and by the pinning/reproduction rule.
- gen_chk_reset: after a mid-run rst_ni assertion, every DUT output is at its reset value in the
  first cycle after release (F-RST-009), the first fetch is the boot vector when fetch is enabled
  (F-RST-002), every response owed for a pre-reset request is DROPPED by the memory model at
  release and none reaches the DUT (F-RST-018; S3 / Q-010: the RTL has no outstanding-request
  qualifier), and the abandoned instruction leaves no RVFI record (F-RST-019). Needed by TP-XIF-017; the
  existing inventory has no reset checker (gen_chk_crash_dump covers only the dump fields).

  so retirement-anchored events are back-dated by one cycle and read cycle-exactly at the pins;
  CSR-write / mret-dret commit cycles are record - 2 / record - 1 (gen_tb_architecture.md 8.2).
  "Same cycle" now names one back-dated cycle per coverpoint (S18); the only windows left are the

- Q-8 RESOLVED (gen_tb_architecture.md 8.3 item 4 / 8.3a; gen_tb_knobs.yaml): the command-line
  forms are the codegen ones only, `+gen_knob_<name>=<value>` (a knob given on the command line is

  no schedule-seed plusarg, no per-agent regime plusarg and no separate pin plusarg. Per-knob

# 4.9 Areas WIT: Cycle-clause witness bins (round-4 medium 1)


The WIT covergroup (fcov_wit.md, CG-WIT-001) has no test-plan items of its own: its bins are owned by the marked
items in the other parts (their Bins lines cite CG-WIT-001.cp_clause.w_<id>). This file exists so the build's area
list stays uniform.
